title: Chachma and the power of speech: metzaref, the five gevuros and the changing combinations
overview: The text explains the power of speech, which he says comes from chachma. Speech is breath, the matter, which the five gevuros of mnatzpach, coming from Ima (bina), cut into letters. Each of the five organs of articulation makes its own letters, and five letters give 120 combinations. One voice joins the letters into words, as a string joins pearls, and thought has the same structure, with a general thought that connects its details. What makes speech flow without effort is chachma: the power of metzaref makes something separate become transparent, as a small child speaks without being taught the movements. That power comes from the koach hamaskil, above bina, and it is why a person is called a speaker, a nefesh hamedabreis, whose letters come from the essence of the soul. The combinations change across the six days of creation, which come from the middos of Malchus of Atzilus, from chesed to din. Our avoda and our perception decide what the changes bring. A tzaddik who understands the combinations can change the meaning of things, and Rabbi Chanina ben Dosa's vinegar burned. Seeing the whole descent from the ratzon of Ein Sof reveals G-d even in nature.

sections.summary: Speech is the breath cut by the five gevuros of mnatzpach, which come from bina and are expressed through the five organs of articulation. Each organ makes its own letters, and the combinations of letters grow fast.

blocks.text: The chapter goes on with *Malchus*, whose main power is externalization: taking an idea that is inside us and bringing it out, as speech turns a thought into words that take on a life of their own. The *Ein Sof* has the same power to make a created world that feels separate from G-d. Today's topic is how this relates to the *koach hametzaref*, the power of joining things together.

The *Tanya* describes speech this way. There is the content of what a person says, and there is the ability to say it: the mouth moves by itself to make the right sounds, and a listener takes in the sounds and understands them without thinking. Something separate becomes transparent and felt as one with us. This is the power of *metzaref* that comes from *chachma*, which joins separate things to the *etzem*.

The five *gevuros* of *mnatzpach* are the five letters that take a different form at the end of a word. Each is a cutting that makes distinctions, and the *gevuros* are what divide one idea into separate parts.

These are the five *gevuros* of *mnatzpach* in the ten utterances, through which G-d creates the world. They make things look separate, like *yesh*, *metzius* and *teva* (nature), instead of a constant *nes*. Everything is really G-d's *ratzon*, which comes through *chachma* into *Malchus* and is created through the ten utterances.

The analogy is a person speaking, who must cut the sound into separate little letters. As said before, the mother lends her garments to the daughter. *Bina* cuts the idea into thoughts, and those thoughts are lent to speech, which gives it its content.
blocks.title: A person speaking

blocks.text: The five *gevuros* from *bina* are expressed through the five organs of articulation: lips, teeth, tongue, palate and throat. Each organ cuts the sound in its own way, so each produces its own letters.

The letters of the throat are the ones that sound *ah, cha, ha* and *ah*. The letters that sound *ge, ye, ke* and *ko* come from the palate. Each speech organ has letters of its own, a whole field of study in linguistics with charts of where each sound is made. Each language makes the sounds slightly differently.

blocks.text: Letters are strung together in many ways to make words. The mouth switches from one part to another, and each sound needs a slightly different setting. That is why tongue twisters are hard: some sounds need opposite motions in the mouth, and unfamiliar combinations are harder still.

The *Sefer Yetzira* says G-d implanted the twenty-two letters in the mouth. They are spiritual, but they become physical motions that carry our ideas. Only one letter is spoken at a time, so each takes its turn as the one in charge.

Letters can be combined in many ways, and the number grows fast; the text calls the combinations houses. Two letters give four combinations, and three give, he asks, six? Five letters give 120, which is the mathematical factorial: multiply the numbers up to the count. The more letters, the more combinations.

blocks.text: The *gevuros* are needed to divide the breath into letters. The breath is the medium, and conveying information needs a medium that can be modulated: the on and off of Morse code or binary, AM radio, which varies the loudness, and FM, which varies the frequency. Here the breath is the medium, and the five *gevuros* cut it into letters.

sections.summary: Speech is the breath, the matter, shaped into letters by the gevuros, and joined by one voice, like a string through pearls. Thought has the same structure, and its voice comes from the gevuros of Ima.

blocks.text: Speech has matter and form. The matter is the breath, which is made of fire, water and wind; its moisture or dryness shapes the sound of the voice. The form is the voice, which is cut into letters, and the letters strung into speech. Breath, voice and speech are three things.

One voice connects all the letters, the way you recognize a person's voice even when they say different words. The emotional state of the speaker colors that voice, so a happy voice or a whiny one sets the general tone, and the tone gives the context: is the speaker happy, angry or sad?
blocks.title: One voice connects all the letters

blocks.text: This is what texting lacks, which is why people add emojis: was I saying it as a joke, seriously, or angrily? Much of that comes through tone of voice and facial features. Communication has many layers, and the voice is what connects the letters to each other.

blocks.text: Thought has letters too, and it has a general thought that surrounds and connects all its details, like a train of thought. Lose it and you don't know what comes next. So with each specific thing you say, you have to have that general thought.

In thought itself there is a spiritual voice: the emotional state that says what you are trying to accomplish, beyond the specifics. In thought this comes from the *gevuros* of *Ima*. In speech it comes in a more physical way, from the five *gevuros* in the organs of articulation.

sections.title: Chachma makes separate things transparent: the power of metzaref in speech
sections.summary: Speech comes from two sources: bina cuts the idea into letters, and chachma makes the letters flow so seamlessly that they feel like part of us. The power of metzaref comes from the hidden chachma, the koach hamaskil.

blocks.text: In understanding, each thing is created by its own *maamar*, but there is also a unifying aspect, a hidden part of everything that unites it all. That is kind of like the *ratzon*, maybe, being expressed in it: the desire to exist and to live.

The combinations come from *bina*, but there is another aspect that comes from *chachma*, which connects everything. *Chachma* is what lets an external medium like speech become completely transparent. A person who speaks well doesn't have to think how to move his lips, and someone who masters an instrument just plays.

*Chachma* is the idea of *bittul* of something separate: creation seems separate, but it is completely transparent to G-d's *ratzon* and wisdom. So the world can be seen as G-d communicating with us. The real power of speech comes from *chachma*: something separate that becomes transparent.

As explained about *machshava*, the letters themselves come from the five *gevuros*, which cut the intellect of speech into parts. First you cut the idea into little thoughts, put each thought into a word, and then say one word at a time.

The combinations follow the *kavana* of what you are trying to convey, so you say what you have in mind. The content of speech is set by the intention in the thought of speech, which dictates exactly what the person says. Sometimes there is a slip, but in general the words change constantly as the intention changes.

We see that as soon as you want to speak, you don't need to analyze with *bina* how to form the sounds. Even a small child who can speak joins words with no preparation, and you don't have to train him specifically how to move his mouth.

It takes time to learn, but not as a conscious process. The deeper part of the brain learns tasks like walking or riding a bike: it wires them in and bypasses conscious thought. Speech is one of these essential things.

Speech comes from *chachma*, where something becomes one with us; *bina*, the ability to label and analyze, is a step removed and sometimes useful. Psychology has names for these two types of thinking, which he does not recall.

This is the *koach hamaskil* itself: the ability to take associated things and fuse them until they are one thing, which is the source of *chachma*. Just as *bina*'s power to cut things up comes from its *makif*, so the power of *chachma* to connect to something separate, like language, art or music, comes from the source of *chachma*.

sections.title: The speaking soul: chachma's power in the letters that come from the essence
sections.summary: A person is called a speaker because speech is the power of chachma that joins the letters to the essence of the soul. Speech reveals G-d's essence in low things, which is the idea of a dira b'tachtonim.

blocks.text: As explained elsewhere, G-d made the first man a living soul, and this is the *ruach memalel*, which has the innermost aspect of the ancient *chachma*. G-d gave us that superior thing, so we are able to speak and are called a speaking spirit. Symbolic representation through language comes from this *koach hamaskil*, the power to make something transparent to the thing itself. That is why speech, art and music are representations of this power given to humans.

Each has its own relationship to *Malchus*: *chachma*, the father who founds the daughter, and *bina*, each playing its part. The content comes from *bina*, and the ability to have it flow seamlessly comes from *chachma*.

blocks.text: The first *maamar*, *Bereishis*, stands for the *chachma* and *sechel* in the *maamarot*, not for the power that connects them. There is a wisdom in speech, the plan by which G-d sets up nature and how everything works. That *chachma* is built into creation: it is the *chachma* of *Bereishis*.

The higher *koach hametzaref* is the general ability to have speech at all and to create things that seem separate, yet are transparent to G-d's *ratzon*. That ability comes from a higher, primordial intellect. Giving a *mashal* also comes from the *koach hamaskil*, since to express something as separate you must understand the idea more deeply. G-d's revealing Himself in what seems separate comes from a higher place.

This is the main idea of *adam*: a person is called a *medaber*, one who speaks. He has a deeper ability, the source of the combining of speech, which is why we are called a *nefesh hamedabreis*. It lets us see G-dliness in the world, and it comes from the source of *chachma*.
The same power lets a person become *batel*, his whole existence nullified to G-d, even though on one hand he is separate. That is this power of *chachma*.

When the source and root of the letters, which come from the essence of the soul, come out into speech, it is called the speaking soul, *ruach memalel*. Through it we can express something from our *etzem* and see the *Or Ein Sof* in things and reveal it. This is the idea of making a *dira b'tachtonim*: revealing G-d's essence in things that seem completely low and separate.

sections.title: The six days: the combinations change with the middos of Malchus
sections.summary: The letters of each day of creation are a different combination from the middos of Malchus of Atzilus: the first day's light is chesed, the second day's firmament is din. The changes follow the light of Abba that founds the daughter, and our own avoda affects what comes.

blocks.text: On the first day, *yehi or*, the letters express *chesed*. That is the source of the first thousand years, when people lived very long, sustained by the kindness of G-d without *Torah*.
The six days correspond to the six *middos* of *Zeir Anpin* and *Nukva*, called *yemei olam* (masculine) and *yemos olam* (feminine).
The second day was different: *yehi rakia* expresses the *din* of *Malchus*, the source of the second thousand years, when there was the flood and the *dor haflaga*.

blocks.text: The changes in the combinations come from the way *chachma* and *bina* flow into the *middos*. Through this, the combinations change by themselves from *chesed* to *din*, in general and in particular.

It also depends on our *avoda*. Had that generation done *teshuva*, the flood would have been a blessing; since they could not make a boat, it was a flood. So the same thing is a blessing or a flood, depending on how we receive it.

All these changes come from the light of *chachma* that founds *Malchus*. The content of what happens comes from *bina*, but how we perceive it, as good or bad, depends on something deeper, a higher *kavana* beyond the light of *chachma*. I think that is the idea here. Seeing a thing as *chesed* or as *din*, and learning from it, comes from the deeper *koach hametzaref* that G-d put in us. That is because G-d gave us this nature to find meaning and see G-dliness in things, since we have a *nefesh Elokis* that resonates with it.

sections.title: Nature is the ratzon of G-d: the ten maamarot reach even the smallest detail
sections.summary: The power of the ten utterances reaches down to details, as the story of Rabbi Chanina ben Dosa shows. A tzaddik who understands the combinations can change the nature of things. Seeing the whole descent from the ratzon of Ein Sof reveals G-d in nature, which is the idea of a dira b'tachtonim.

blocks.text: Rabbi Chanina ben Dosa's daughter put vinegar into the Shabbos candles by accident instead of oil, and did not know what to do. He said that whoever said oil should burn should say that vinegar should burn. The one who gave oil its nature through the ten utterances of the Name Elokim can attach that nature to vinegar, and it will burn. This is how far the change can come down, to the very details of things.

blocks.text: On a simple level, this is even the idea of the sciences: normally heavy pieces of metal do not fly, but once you understand the deeper *chachma* of how things work, you can build a plane. A *tzaddik* who understands how G-d creates the world and how the combinations work can look at any situation from a different perspective and change its meaning.

In *Masechta Taanis* it talks about a tragedy turned into a springboard for something good, by changing oneself and one's perspective. I think that is what he means here: a *tzaddik* rules over the 120 combinations of *Elokim* with his fear of G-d, since a five-letter word has 120.

blocks.text: The main thing in this rule is changing the *mochin* of *Nukva*: *chachma* and *bina* of the ten *maamarot*, which come from the source of *chachma* and the source of the *ratzon*.

Looking deeper at the inner meaning and purpose of things reveals the hidden good in everything, as *Tanya* says, and *emunah* helps reveal it. I think this is a similar idea to what he is talking about here.

It starts with seeing the deeper possibility, not seeing oneself as a victim. A challenge like the flood can be met by looking deeper and building the boat: that brings out the potential inside us, and it changes things into real success.

phrases.en: like it says, that everything that G-d desires He does
this is the idea of being able to, that the *maamarot* externally are making everything seem separate

phrases.he: בבחינת עשיה דמלכות דאצילות הנזכר לעיל

blocks.text: Everything G-d desires, He does. The *maamarot* make things seem separate, but it is really G-d's *ratzon*, higher than that. Like a miracle, it comes from G-d: *ein od milvado*, there is nothing else besides Him.

Nature was made through the ten *maamarot*, which hide G-d. Their purpose is to reveal G-d's *koach hagevul*, a revelation of the *Ein Sof*: nature and the *yetzer hara* can be seen in a new light that reveals G-d. That is a *dira b'tachtonim*.

G-d's *ratzon*, which is higher than *sechel*, *taam*, *daas* and *teva*, is what is revealed in the ten *maamarot* of the supernal speech of *Atzilus*. It comes down to *Asiya* and *Malchus* of *Atzilus*, and from there all the way down, as we will see.

phrases.he: ומכל זה יובן גם כן בחינת כללות ההתבוננות
phrases.en: and from this, we can also understand another *hisbonenus* that we can make from the top to the bottom

phrases.he: ברבוי פרטים, דהיינו ממקור הרצון שבמלכות דאין סוף עד מלכות דמלכות דאצילות, עד סוף מעשה ממש, להיות כל אשר חפץ יהו״ה עשה בפו"מ, כמו שהחומץ ידליק בפועל ממש וכהאי גוונא ודי למבין

blocks.text: Another *hisbonenus*: from the *ratzon* in the *Malchus* of *Ein Sof* down to the *Malchus* of *Malchus* of *Atzilus*, to the end of the actual deed. Nature and the world all come from the *Malchus* of *Ein Sof*.
The *tzimtzum* reveals that G-d, who is *Ein Sof*, also has the power of *gevul* to create limited things, so the world and nature look separate but are all His *ratzon*.
The very limited thing, hidden in the *reshimu*, is really the whole *koach ha'Ein Sof*, even though it seems very limited.

The more we look deeper, the more possibilities we find, expressing G-d's *ratzon*. This makes *nissim* possible, clothed in nature, like the sciences and technology, or higher than it. This *hisbonenus* sees the *koach ha'Ein Sof* coming down even into *gevul*: a *dira b'tachtonim*.

reviewQuestions.question: Where do the letters of speech come from, and what cuts the breath into them?
What is the difference between the content of speech and the power that lets it flow without effort?
How do the six days of creation relate to the changing combinations of letters?
What does the story of Rabbi Chanina ben Dosa and the vinegar show about the combinations?
What does our avoda have to do with how the combinations change?
What is seeing G-d's ratzon in nature, and what does it mean to make a dira b'tachtonim?
